module_title: The Laws of Thermodynamics and Entropy
introduction: Thermodynamics is the study of heat, work, and the laws governing their conversion. These are the absolute, unbreakable rules of the universe that dictate how engines, refrigerators, and the universe itself operate.

core_concepts.title: Zeroth Law of Thermodynamics
core_concepts.description:
If body A is in thermal equilibrium with body B, and body B is in thermal equilibrium with body C, then A and C must be in thermal equilibrium with each other. 
Application: This law forms the basic principle for creating and using 'Thermometers'.

core_concepts.title: First Law (Law of Conservation of Energy)
core_concepts.description:
Heat energy supplied to a system ($dQ$) is equal to the sum of the increase in its internal energy ($dU$) and the external work done by the system ($dW$). 
Formula: $dQ = dU + dW$. 
Meaning: Energy cannot be created or destroyed, only transformed.

core_concepts.title: Second Law and Entropy
core_concepts.description:
This law dictates the 'direction' of heat flow. 
1. Clausius Statement: Heat cannot flow from a colder body to a hotter body without external work (How a refrigerator works). 
2. Kelvin-Planck Statement: It is impossible to build a heat engine that is 100% efficient. Some heat is always wasted to the surroundings. 
Entropy: The measure of randomness or disorder in a system. The universe's total entropy is always increasing.

core_concepts.title: Third Law of Thermodynamics
core_concepts.description: As the temperature of a system approaches Absolute Zero (0 Kelvin), its entropy approaches a constant minimum. Practically, this means 'Absolute Zero is impossible to reach'.

important_entities.name: Adiabatic Process
important_entities.significance: A thermodynamic process where a system changes its state (pressure, volume, temp) but NO heat ($dQ = 0$) enters or leaves the system. Examples: Sudden bursting of a tire, propagation of sound waves in air.

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: Exam Trap: Can a heat engine have an efficiency of 1? NEVER. Even an ideal 'Carnot Engine' cannot have 100% efficiency unless the heat sink is at Absolute Zero (0 K), which is practically impossible.

mnemonics_and_tricks.memory_phrase: 0th = You must play. 1st = You can't win, only break even. 2nd = You can't even break even. 3rd = You can't leave the game.
mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: This famous analogy perfectly summarizes the 4 laws: Definition of Temp (0th), Conservation (1st), Inevitable loss/Entropy (2nd), and Unreachable Absolute Zero (3rd).

exam_strategy_tips: NDA/CDS Questions: 'Which law of thermodynamics introduced the concept of Entropy?' Answer: The Second Law.
